title: Regional Throttle Orchestrator and Soft Reopen Hotfix
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce regional throttle orchestrator, soft reopen gating, eviction dampener, telemetry-gated circuit reopen. Feature-flagged rollout and immediate revert script included.
description: Context: During a partial regional recovery on 2026-02-14 we observed repeated circuit flips and large-scale tenant evictions when a previously degraded region began accepting traffic. These oscillations amplified transient latency spikes and violated short-term SLO budgets for multiple customers. Motivation: introduce a coordinated, conservative reopen flow to avoid mass preemption and provide an automated safe rollback path. Changes: 1) runtime/failover/regional_orchestrator: new lightweight orchestrator that manages reopen epochs and issues transient 'soft-reopen' tokens to nodes in a region; tokens constrain allowed parallel rejoin rate and expose an observed-health window. 2) controller/circuit: CircuitController now respects a telemetry_gate which requires k consistent healthy samples (configurable) before upgrading a soft reopen to full open. 3) eviction/service: eviction queue uses a sliding-window penalty-decay and an emergency dampener that defers aggressive preemptions during a reopen epoch. 4) feature flag: regional_throttle_v2 feature-flag guarding behavior; defaults off. 5) scripts/revert-regional-throttle.sh: one-command revert to previous rollout and flag state. Design notes: orchestrator is intentionally single-shard per-region and communicates via existing control-plane pubsub; tokens carry an epoch id and a suggested concurrency cap. The telemetry_gate aggregates latency and error-rate histograms from local probes rather than raw counters to reduce reactivity to noisy samples. Rollout plan: (a) merge behind feature-flag, (b) enable for 10% of clusters in us-west-2 for 6h, monitor eviction-rate, circuit flip rate, and token exhaustion metrics, (c) expand to 50% then 100% if stable. Revert: run scripts/revert-regional-throttle.sh and monitor for immediate restoration of prior behavior. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, integration harness that simulates region flap with controlled RTT and error spike, canary run in staging with 3 clusters. Observability: new metrics regional_orchestrator.epoch_duration, regional_orchestrator.token_grants, circuit.telemetry_gate_samples, eviction.dampener_deferrals added to dashboard and log keys prefixed with rto:. Backwards compat: when flag is off or orchestrator unreachable system falls back to existing per-node reopen logic. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e canary in staging, [x] docs + rollout notes, [x] revert script, [x] security scan. Rationale: this balances safety and liveness during region recoveries and reduces tenant-impacting evictions while keeping the control plane in charge of reopen pacing.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Design LGTM. Two questions: (1) can we avoid additional control plane load during large-scale reopens? (2) what's the failure mode if orchestrator loses quorum?

Maya Chen (reply): Orchestrator is single-shard per-region and uses existing pubsub; token grants are rate-limited and cached to minimize chatter. If orchestrator becomes unreachable we fallback to per-node local reopen with a conservative backoff (documented).
Priya Nair: Please add a metric that counts 'soft-reopen to full-open transitions' and expose it to SLO dashboard — I want to watch conversion rate during canary.
Maya Chen (reply): Added metric circuit.telemetry_gate_samples and a derived metric rto.soft_to_full_transitions; dashboard updated.
Lars Petersen: Found a race in the token expiry path, flagged a small fix in last commit — re-running tests now.
